content.text:
I migrated all three lodash calls to es-toolkit. The result is in `out/module.ts`, and it type-checks under `tsc --strict --skipLibCheck`. I couldn't compare it against the original, because lodash isn't installed in the project.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 816 bytes (min+gzip), with 100 bytes of my own code. I didn't measure the original's size, so I can't say how close that is to the smallest reachable size or to the own-code allowance.

| Function | es-toolkit replacement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `toSlug` | `kebabCase` from `es-toolkit/string` | Digit and uppercase-run splitting matches lodash's usual output ("max44_id" gives "max-44-id", "ABCdef" gives "ab-cdef"). |
| `byNameKey` | `keyBy` from `es-toolkit/array`, with `(r) => r.name` as the key function | The main-package `keyBy` takes a function instead of the `'name'` string, so I used a one-line arrow function. For duplicate names, the last row wins. |
| `preview` | `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat` | The main package (v1.53.2) has no `truncate`, and `compat` is its lodash-compatible one. |

I didn't keep a lodash import, since es-toolkit covers all three.

- **Checked by running:** the `kebabCase` cases above and `truncate` on a short string and a 40-character string.
- **Checked only by reading:** `preview`'s exact output for longer inputs, since I had no lodash output to diff against.
- **Export compatibility:** the `Row` and `Config` exports and all three function signatures are unchanged.
